answer: Glacier-paced admission gates each new identity behind a minimum inter-arrival delay measured against a rolling median of peer registration intervals. Agents whose arrival cadence falls below that floor are queued until the delay elapses, and their first messages must pass an echo check: the reply latency pattern is compared to the arrival shape. A quill log records each arrival timestamp permanently, so an attacker must spread registrations across real elapsed time and pay cloud costs for idle waiting periods per identity.
